farms.name: General Mob Farm (dark tower)
farms.principle: Dark spawning platforms high in the sky (or over the void of a lit area) let only hostile mobs spawn; water streams push them to a central fall/lava kill and hoppers collect drops.
farms.y_level: 128+ (or 24+ blocks above surrounding, spawn-proof caves nearby)
caveats: Spawn-proof all caves within 128 blocks or the hostile mob cap (70) starves the farm.

farms.name: Creeper Farm (cat-filtered)
farms.principle: A tall dark platform where cats scare away all non-creeper mobs, so only creepers spawn; they drop to a controlled kill for pure gunpowder.
caveats: Charged creepers can destroy the build during thunderstorms unless roofed.

farms.name: Dungeon Spawner XP Farm
farms.principle: A natural monster spawner (zombie/skeleton/spider) is enclosed and dark; mobs are washed into a 1-hit kill chamber for fast early-game XP and drops.
caveats: Rate is capped by the single spawner; best as an early-game XP source.

farms.name: Enderman Ender Pearl / XP Farm (End)
farms.principle: On the main End island / outer islands endermen spawn densely; an endermite (or player) lures them to a two-block-high kill spot where they take fatal fall/hit damage for huge XP and ender pearls.
farms.rate: very high XP + stacks of pearls/h
caveats: Endermen teleport if they touch water/rain; use a dry enclosed platform.

farms.name: Nether Roof Gold Farm (zombified piglin)
farms.principle: Zombified piglins spawn on nether-roof platforms; they are funneled to a 1-hit kill for gold nuggets/ingots and XP. Spawns are not limited by the hostile mob cap in the same way as portal spawns.
farms.y_level: on the nether roof (y=128) or a large spawn plane
farms.rate: very high XP + many gold ingots/h
caveats: Requires access to the nether roof or a very large spawn plane; light every other surface for 128 blocks.

farms.name: Piglin Bartering Farm
farms.principle: Adult piglins are held on a platform and given gold ingots by a dispenser; their barter drops fall through to storage, yielding ender pearls, obsidian, and more from a renewable gold supply.
farms.rate: barter-rate limited by gold input (~1 barter/pig/6-8s)
caveats: Pair with a gold farm for a renewable input; piglins must stand on a non-full block or netherrack/soul-sand and not zombify (keep in Nether).

farms.name: Blaze Farm (nether fortress spawner)
farms.principle: A nether-fortress blaze spawner is boxed in; blazes are pushed by water (or trapped) into a kill spot for blaze rods, essential for brewing and eyes of ender.
caveats: Water only exists near the spawner via placement adjacent to the fortress structure; blazes are fire-immune so use fall/hits, not lava.

farms.name: Wither Skeleton Farm (fortress)
farms.principle: Nether-fortress spawn spaces are spawn-proofed except a dark platform where wither skeletons spawn; they fall to a kill spot yielding coal, bones, and rare skulls for the Wither.
caveats: Wither skeletons only spawn inside the fortress bounding box; spawn-proof the whole fortress except the platform.

farms.name: Guardian / Elder Guardian Farm (ocean monument)
farms.principle: The whole ocean monument's water is drained/reserved as the spawn area; guardians spawn in the monument water volume and are flushed down to a kill spot for prismarine, crystals and cod.
caveats: Large water-clearing project (sponges/drainage). Guardians need the monument water volume to spawn.

farms.name: Raid Farm (emeralds + totems)
farms.principle: A villager with Bad Omen triggers repeated raids in a controlled arena; raiders are funneled to a kill spot, dropping emeralds and (from evokers) totems of undying.
farms.y_level: high in sky to avoid stray spawns
caveats: Raid trigger and Bad Omen handling changed with the Trial Chambers update (ominous bottles). Build above y=high and spawn-proof to avoid raider scatter.

farms.name: Iron Golem Farm (villager panic)
farms.principle: Three+ villagers with beds and a nearby threat (zombie) panic and summon iron golems on a spawn platform; golems fall/are pushed to a lava/kill spot for guaranteed 3-5 iron each.
farms.y_level: any (build in sky to avoid caps)
caveats: Since 1.21.2 villagers detect existing golems up to ~45 blocks and stop spawning; keep modules 64+ blocks apart and don't leave stray golems nearby (MC-277889).

farms.name: Drowned Farm (river/ocean spawn)
farms.principle: Drowned spawn in open river/ocean water below sea level; they are funneled to a kill spot for tridents, nautilus shells, and copper/rotten flesh. (Not the zombie-conversion type.)
caveats: Only naturally-spawned drowned drop tridents/shells; zombie-converted drowned do not. River biome gives best rates.

farms.name: Witch Farm (swamp hut)
farms.principle: A swamp witch hut spawns witches in its bounding box regardless of other spawns when the area is spawn-proofed; witches fall to a kill spot for redstone, glowstone, gunpowder, and sugar.
caveats: Spawn-proof the whole 128-block area so witch-hut spawns dominate; fall damage must exceed witch self-heal or use a player hit.

farms.name: Slime Farm (swamp)
farms.principle: Slimes spawn in swamp biomes between y=50-70 at night; a flat lit-controlled platform gathers them to a kill for slime balls.
caveats: Swamp slime spawns only 50<=y<=70, light<=7 and at night; slime-chunk farms are the deep alternative.

farms.name: Slime Farm (slime chunk, deep)
farms.principle: In a slime chunk below y=40, slimes spawn regardless of light; several floors are dug out and lit for AFK, with slimes pushed to a kill.
caveats: Requires locating a slime chunk; dig 3+ floors and light caves within 128 blocks to reduce competing spawns.

farms.name: Spider Farm (string)
farms.principle: A dark 3-wide spawning floor lets spiders spawn; sloped/ trapdoor tricks move them to a kill for string and spider eyes.
caveats: Spiders need a 3x3 footprint to spawn and climb walls; use overhangs/trapdoors to prevent escape.

farms.name: Cave Spider Spawner Farm
farms.principle: A mineshaft cave-spider spawner is enclosed; tiny cave spiders are washed to a 1-tall kill gap for fast string, eyes, and XP.
caveats: Cave spiders are 1 block tall and poison; use a half-slab kill gap and drink milk if hit.

farms.name: Zombie Spawner Farm
farms.principle: A dungeon zombie spawner feeds a water channel into a kill chamber for rotten flesh (emerald trading with villagers) and early XP.
caveats: Rotten flesh trades to cleric villagers for emeralds; rare iron/carrot/potato drops from equipped zombies.

farms.name: Trial Spawner Loot/XP Cycle (Trial Chamber)
farms.principle: Trial spawners eject loot after each wave and have a 30-min cooldown, so you cycle through a chamber's many spawners; ominous mode (ominous bottle) upgrades keys/loot and drops the heavy core.
farms.rate: per-cooldown cycle; heavy core ~7.5% per ominous vault
caveats: Trial spawners cannot be moved and have a 30-min cooldown; cycle multiple spawners. Vaults unlock once per player.

farms.name: Breeze Rod Farm (trial spawner)
farms.principle: Breeze trial spawners are cleared repeatedly; breezes drop breeze rods (for wind charges / crafting) and the fight yields keys.
caveats: Breeze rods only come from breeze trial spawners; deflect wind charges. No fully-AFK design (trial spawner requires a player).

farms.name: Phantom Farm (membrane)
farms.principle: A player who hasn't slept for 3+ days lures phantoms into a boxed kill area; phantoms drop membranes for elytra repair and slow-falling potions.
caveats: Requires staying awake (insomnia). Phantoms only spawn under open sky above the player.

farms.name: Shulker Farm (End city dupe)
farms.principle: A captured shulker in an End city is induced to spawn a new shulker when its bullet hits another shulker; the offspring is collected for a self-sustaining shulker shell supply.
caveats: Needs a starter shulker pair; shells require killing offspring only (keep breeders alive).

farms.name: Hoglin Farm (crimson forest)
farms.principle: Hoglins breed with crimson fungi; babies grow and are pushed to a cooked-kill (fire/lava-adjacent) for cooked porkchop and leather.
caveats: Hoglins flee from warped fungi/nylium and portals; keep the pen clear of repellents.

farms.name: Sculk / Warden-free XP via mob deaths on catalyst
farms.principle: Mobs are killed on top of a sculk catalyst so their XP is converted into sculk blocks and sculk sensors/shriekers material, farming sculk for building and redstone.
caveats: Needs a starter sculk catalyst from the Deep Dark; mobs must die within range of the catalyst to convert XP.

farms.name: Cobblestone Generator
farms.principle: Lava meeting flowing water forms cobblestone in a fixed spot; a piston or auto-miner breaks it and hoppers collect, giving unlimited cobblestone.
caveats: Fastest designs use an observer-piston clock; keep the generation block isolated so only cobblestone forms.

farms.name: Stone Generator
farms.principle: Lava flowing onto a source of water forms stone (not cobblestone) when the flow direction is controlled; auto-mined for smooth building stone without smelting.
caveats: Stone (vs cobble) forms only when lava flows over a still-water source in the correct geometry.

farms.name: Cobbled Deepslate Generator
farms.principle: Lava + water generation performed below y=0 (or with deepslate as the base) yields cobbled deepslate for dark building stock.
caveats: Deepslate variant forms when the generation replaces a deepslate block; otherwise you get cobblestone.

farms.name: Basalt Generator
farms.principle: Lava next to soul soil with blue ice adjacent forms basalt; a piston array breaks and collects it for unlimited basalt building blocks.
caveats: Requires the exact lava/soul-soil/blue-ice geometry; works in any dimension.

farms.name: Obsidian Farm (auto pump)
farms.principle: Water is pumped onto a controlled lava source to form obsidian in a fixed slot, which is then mined; automated variants use dispensers and a diamond/netherite auto-miner is manual.
caveats: Obsidian must be pickaxe-mined (no piston harvest); the farm only automates reformation of the lava slot.

farms.name: Sand Duper (TNT duplication)
farms.principle: A TNT duplicator repeatedly blows a column of falling sand, which is duplicated by the entity-in-portal / dupe mechanic and collected — the standard technical source of bulk sand.
caveats: Relies on TNT/sand duplication, a technical (glitch-based) mechanic that some servers/anti-cheats disable; verify it is allowed on your world.

farms.name: Gravel Duper (TNT duplication)
farms.principle: Same gravity-block duplication as the sand duper but with gravel, giving bulk gravel (and flint via crafting/trades).
caveats: Duplication-based; disabled on many servers. Flint comes from crafting gravel or trading, not directly.

farms.name: Auto Concrete Converter
farms.principle: Concrete powder is dropped into water to harden into concrete, then a piston/auto-miner breaks and collects it — turning bulk sand+gravel+dye into building concrete.
caveats: Pairs with a sand duper for endless concrete; any of the 16 colors works with the matching powder.

farms.name: Froglight Farm
farms.principle: Frogs eat small magma cubes and produce froglights; frog variant (temperate/warm/cold, set by the biome they grow up in) determines ochre/pearlescent/verdant.
caveats: Frog variant is fixed by the biome the tadpole grows up in (warm->pearlescent, cold->verdant, temperate->ochre). Needs a small-magma-cube supply.

farms.name: Amethyst Farm (budding grow-and-mine)
farms.principle: Amethyst clusters grow on budding amethyst; a flying-machine/piston-slime auto-miner (or manual) harvests the fully-grown clusters for shards.
farms.y_level: geode depth (or relocated buds not possible)
caveats: Budding amethyst cannot be moved (drops nothing), so the farm is built around an existing geode. Fully-grown clusters must be broken without silk touch for shards.

farms.name: Ice Farm (freeze cycle)
farms.principle: Water sources freeze into ice in a cold/snowy biome (or under an open sky at high y in cold biomes); a piston/auto-miner harvests ice, then water reflows to refreeze.
farms.y_level: high, open sky in cold biome
caveats: Water only freezes in cold biomes with light level <=11 and open sky; ice mined without silk touch yields nothing, so break to item requires care (use silk-touch harvester or collect as full ice via piston).

farms.name: Snow Farm (snow golem)
farms.principle: A snow golem trapped in a cold biome leaves a snow-layer trail; a piston or shovel-dispenser harvests the layers into snowballs for endless snow blocks.
caveats: Snow golem only leaves a trail in cold-enough biomes; keep it out of warm biomes (it melts) and rain.

farms.name: Pointed Dripstone Farm
farms.principle: Pointed dripstone on a dripstone block with a water source above grows downward over time; a piston breaks the grown tips for dripstone used in lava/pointed-dripstone builds.
caveats: Growth is random-tick slow; used mainly to feed lava/water dripstone farms.

farms.name: Lava Farm (dripstone + cauldron)
farms.principle: A pointed dripstone under a lava source slowly fills a cauldron below with lava; many stations give a renewable lava supply for fuel and building.
farms.rate: very slow per station; scale wide
caveats: Only one drip station fills one cauldron slowly; renewable but low rate. Great fuel source with no nether trips.

farms.name: Clay Farm (mud + dripstone)
farms.principle: Mud placed above a pointed dripstone (with no water below the tip) slowly drips and converts to clay; automated placement/harvest gives renewable clay for bricks and terracotta.
caveats: Mud is made from dirt + water bottle; conversion needs a pointed dripstone directly below the mud with air (no water) beneath the tip.

farms.name: Sugar Cane Farm (observer harvest)
farms.principle: Each cane grows to 3 tall; an observer facing the top block detects growth and fires a piston to break the cane, which floats to a water channel and hoppers.
caveats: Cane needs water adjacent to the base sand/dirt; observers on the middle block avoid breaking un-grown cane.

farms.name: Bamboo Farm (observer harvest)
farms.principle: Bamboo grows fast and tall; an observer detects growth at a set height and a piston breaks it for fuel, scaffolding, and composter/bonemeal input.
caveats: Bamboo needs light>=9. Great fuel (crafted to bamboo planks/sticks) and composter feedstock.

farms.name: Cactus Farm
farms.principle: Cactus breaks itself when it grows next to a block; the dropped cactus floats along water into hoppers with zero redstone.
caveats: Cactus needs sand and an empty diagonal; smelt cactus for green dye, or use for a passive XP/trash design.

farms.name: Melon Farm (observer/piston)
farms.principle: Melon stems grow melons into a fixed slot; an observer detects the melon and a piston breaks it into a water channel for slices/seeds and emerald trades.
caveats: Stems must have a free dirt/farmland slot to grow the melon into; light>=9.

farms.name: Pumpkin Farm (observer/piston)
farms.principle: Pumpkin stems grow pumpkins into a slot watched by an observer; a piston breaks them for pumpkins (carved pumpkins, pie, emeralds, snow/iron golems).
caveats: Same as melon; pumpkins are the input for carved pumpkins/golems and strong emerald trades.

farms.name: Villager Wheat Farm
farms.principle: A farmer villager plants and harvests wheat automatically; excess he can't pick up falls through to a hopper-minecart under the farmland.
caveats: Give the villager a composter to make him a farmer; a hopper-minecart under the farmland collects overflow.

farms.name: Villager Carrot/Potato Farm
farms.principle: Same villager-farming loop but planted with carrots or potatoes; a huge food source for breeders, trades, and rabbit/pig breeding.
caveats: Carrots/potatoes feed villager breeders and make golden carrots; rare poisonous potato drops mixed in.

farms.name: Villager Beetroot Farm
farms.principle: Villager-farmed beetroot for soup, red dye, and trades; collected via hopper-minecart under the plots.
caveats: Villagers won't replant beetroot as eagerly as wheat/carrot; keep seeds in the loop.

farms.name: Kelp Farm (dried kelp fuel)
farms.principle: Kelp grows upward in water; an observer at a set height and a piston break the column, dropped kelp is collected and smelted to dried kelp blocks (great furnace fuel).
caveats: 9 dried kelp craft into a dried kelp block, a renewable fuel; the piston breaks the top so lower kelp keeps growing.

farms.name: Nether Wart Farm
farms.principle: Nether wart grows on soul sand; a piston-flush or water-dispenser harvest (water works with soul sand) breaks all mature wart into collection.
caveats: Essential for brewing. Water placed via dispenser on soul sand flushes wart without removing the soul sand.

farms.name: Cocoa Bean Farm
farms.principle: Cocoa pods grow on jungle logs; a piston/flying-machine breaks mature pods for cocoa beans (brown dye, cookies).
caveats: Cocoa must be planted on jungle logs; only mature (dark) pods drop 3 beans.

farms.name: Sweet Berry Farm (piston harvest)
farms.principle: Sweet berry bushes grow berries; a piston/flying-machine bumps the bushes to pop the berries into water/hoppers for food and fox breeding.
caveats: Berries are picked by breaking/bumping the bush at growth stage 2-3; also a passive mob-damage barrier.

farms.name: Glow Berry Farm (cave vines)
farms.principle: Cave vines grow downward and produce glow berries; an observer detects berries and a piston/flush harvests them for food and free light.
caveats: Glow berries plant cave vines and emit light 14; only berried vines drop berries when broken.

farms.name: Chorus Fruit Farm (End)
farms.principle: Chorus flowers grow chorus plants on end stone; breaking the base with a piston/flying-machine collapses the whole plant into drops of chorus fruit and flowers.
caveats: Chorus flowers only grow on end stone; breaking the bottom block drops the entire plant. Popped chorus fruit = purpur.

farms.name: Mushroom Farm (dark spread)
farms.principle: Red/brown mushrooms spread to nearby valid blocks at light<=12; a piston/flush harvests the spread mushrooms for stew, dyes, and huge-mushroom bonemeal builds.
caveats: Mushrooms spread only in low light; mycelium/podzol/nylium let them survive any light. Also grow huge mushrooms with bone meal for bulk.

farms.name: Moss Farm (bone meal spread)
farms.principle: Bone meal on a moss block spreads moss to adjacent blocks and grows azalea/plants; a piston-based converter turns cheap blocks into moss, then into dirt/roots products.
caveats: Pairs with a bone-meal (bamboo/kelp composter) farm; converts stone/dirt into moss for terraforming.

farms.name: Flower / Dye Farm (bone meal)
farms.principle: Bone meal used on grass blocks in a flower-rich biome spawns flowers; a piston/flush sweeps them into hoppers for a full palette of dyes.
caveats: Which flowers appear depends on the biome (flower forest gives the widest variety).

farms.name: Bone Meal Farm (composter)
farms.principle: A fast plant farm (bamboo/kelp/cactus/sugar cane) feeds composters, which convert plant matter into bone meal — a renewable bone-meal engine for other farms.
caveats: A hopper above a composter auto-fills it; a hopper below pulls the bone meal. Feed with any bulk plant matter.

farms.name: Sniffer Ancient Plant Farm
farms.principle: Bred sniffers dig up torchflower and pitcher-pod seeds from moss/dirt; the seeds are grown for decorative plants and dyes, sustaining more sniffers.
caveats: Sniffers dig on moss/dirt-family blocks with a cooldown; breed with torchflower seeds. Decorative/collector farm.

farms.name: Oak Tree Farm (bone meal / observer)
farms.principle: Saplings are force-grown with dispensed bone meal, then a piston/flying-machine or TNT layer chops the trunk; logs, apples, and saplings are collected.
caveats: Oak has variable trunk height; dispensers of bone meal + a full-height chopper handle the randomness. Oak also drops apples.

farms.name: Birch Tree Farm
farms.principle: Birch grows to a fixed height, making it ideal for compact bone-meal + observer/piston auto-choppers with very consistent yields.
caveats: Fixed-height birch makes the most reliable fully-automatic tree farm.

farms.name: Spruce Giant (2x2) Tree Farm
farms.principle: 2x2 spruce saplings grow into giant trees; a flying-machine of pistons+slime sweeps up the huge trunk for the highest logs-per-hour of any wood farm.
caveats: 2x2 giant spruce yields the most wood; needs vertical clearance and a reliable flying machine.

farms.name: Jungle Giant (2x2) Tree Farm
farms.principle: 2x2 jungle saplings grow into tall trees (also the cocoa host); a flying machine chops the trunk for jungle logs at high volume.
caveats: Jungle saplings have a low sapling drop rate, so keep a buffer; 2x2 gives big trees.

farms.name: Acacia Tree Farm
farms.principle: Acacia grows at diagonal angles, so farms use a wide catch area with a flying-machine or layered pistons to harvest the scattered canopy and trunk.
caveats: Acacia's diagonal growth makes harvesting messy; a wide flying-machine sweep is the standard solution.

farms.name: Dark Oak (2x2) Tree Farm
farms.principle: Dark oak only grows from 2x2 saplings; a compact bone-meal + flying-machine design gives dense dark-oak logs plus apples.
caveats: Requires 2x2 saplings (won't grow as singles); drops apples like oak.

farms.name: Mangrove Tree Farm
farms.principle: Mangrove propagules grow into trees (even over water); bone meal + a piston/flying-machine harvest gives logs, roots, and mud (via muddy mangrove roots).
caveats: Mangrove can grow on mud/over water; roots + water bottle make mud, feeding the clay farm.

farms.name: Cherry Tree Farm
farms.principle: Cherry saplings grow into pink-canopy trees; bone meal + observer/piston harvest yields cherry logs and pink petals for decoration.
caveats: Cherry leaves drop pink petals only when sheared/decayed; logs harvest like other single-sapling trees.

farms.name: Pale Oak Tree Farm (Pale Garden)
farms.principle: Pale oak (from the Pale Garden) grows from 2x2 saplings with bone meal; a flying-machine harvest gives pale oak logs and (with the creaking heart) resin.
caveats: Pale oak needs 2x2 saplings; harvest saplings from the Pale Garden first. Resin is a separate creaking-heart product.

farms.name: Crimson Stem Farm (huge fungus)
farms.principle: A crimson fungus on crimson nylium is bone-mealed into a huge fungus; a piston/TNT chopper harvests crimson stems, shroomlight, and nether wart blocks.
caveats: Warped/crimson stems are the only fireproof 'wood'; a warped-nylium block adjacent can stunt growth, so isolate the fungus.

farms.name: Warped Stem Farm (huge fungus)
farms.principle: A warped fungus on warped nylium is bone-mealed into a huge fungus; harvest yields warped stems, shroomlight, and warped wart blocks for cyan builds.
caveats: Warped fungi are safe from piglin aggression zones; harvest the same way as crimson.

farms.name: Charcoal Super Smelter
farms.principle: Logs from a tree farm are fed into a furnace array; a portion of output charcoal is looped back as fuel, making a self-sustaining charcoal engine.
caveats: Feed with any logs; loop a fraction of the charcoal back as fuel so it never runs dry. Furnaces (not blast) are needed to smelt logs into charcoal.

farms.name: Cow Farm (auto beef + leather)
farms.principle: Cows are auto-bred with wheat; adults are pushed by water/piston onto a campfire or lava blade that cooks them, dropping cooked beef and leather into hoppers.
caveats: Separate adults from babies; a campfire cooks the beef so no extra smelting is needed. Feed with a wheat farm.

farms.name: Chicken Farm (auto egg + cooked chicken)
farms.principle: Adult chickens on a slab lay eggs collected by a hopper; a dispenser throws eggs to hatch chicks below, which grow and are cooked by lava above the collection hopper.
caveats: Self-sustaining: eggs from the top layer feed the dispenser that spawns the next generation. Lava must not touch the adults.

farms.name: Pig Farm (porkchop)
farms.principle: Pigs are bred with carrots/potatoes; adults are pushed to a fire/lava kill for cooked porkchop, a simple bulk food source.
caveats: Feed with carrots/potatoes/beetroot; same layout as the cow cooker.

farms.name: Auto Wool Farm (sheep + dispenser shears)
farms.principle: A dyed sheep eats grass to regrow wool; a dispenser with shears clips it automatically on a redstone clock, giving endless colored wool.
caveats: Sheep must stand on grass to regrow wool; dye the sheep for a specific color (or breed for patterns).

farms.name: Rabbit Farm (hide + foot)
farms.principle: Rabbits are bred with carrots; adults are pushed to a kill for rabbit hide (leather), meat, and the rare rabbit's foot.
caveats: 4 rabbit hide craft into 1 leather; rabbit's foot (brewing) is a rare drop.

farms.name: Bee Farm (honey + honeycomb)
farms.principle: Bees pollinate nearby flowers and fill hives to honey_level 5; dispensers with glass bottles (honey) and shears (honeycomb) auto-harvest without angering bees (campfire under the hive).
caveats: A campfire (with a carpet on top to stop fire) under the hive prevents bees from getting angry when harvested; needs flowers nearby to pollinate.

farms.name: Mooshroom Stew Farm
farms.principle: A mooshroom is milked with bowls (dispenser) for mushroom stew, or fed a flower then milked for suspicious stew; an endless renewable food source with zero killing.
caveats: Only mooshrooms (from Mushroom Fields) give stew; feeding a specific flower before milking makes a matching suspicious stew effect.

farms.name: Turtle Scute Farm
farms.principle: Turtles bred with seagrass lay eggs on their home beach sand; babies grow up and drop turtle scute (for the turtle helmet) which is collected.
caveats: Turtles only lay on the sand of their 'home' beach; babies drop 1 scute each when they mature. 5 scute = turtle helmet.

farms.name: Goat Horn Farm
farms.principle: A goat is made to ram a hard block on a redstone-timed lure; the impact drops a goat horn, cycled for all 8 horn variants.
caveats: Goats ram a target every 30-300s onto certain hard blocks; a screaming goat rams far more often. Horn variant is random.

farms.name: AFK Fishing Farm
farms.principle: A held/auto-clicked fishing rod over a 1x1 open-water hole catches fish, junk, and enchanted treasure; drops are funneled by water into a hopper.
caveats: Needs 'open water' (a valid ring of water/air) for treasure; requires a held or auto right-click. Rates were reduced from the old 1.13-era designs.

farms.name: Squid / Glow Squid Ink Farm
farms.principle: Squid spawn in a dark water box (or glow squid below y=30); they are flushed to a kill for ink sacs (black dye) or glow ink sacs (glowing signs).
farms.y_level: glow squid below y=30 in the dark
caveats: Glow squid need light 0 and y<30; regular squid need a water volume. Ink sac = black dye; glow ink sac makes signs glow.

farms.name: Villager Breeder
farms.principle: Two villagers with surplus food (carrots/potatoes/bread) and access to beds breed; baby villagers are transported out to stock trading halls, iron farms, and raid farms.
caveats: Villagers need enough food in inventory and a claimed bed each to breed; feed from a villager crop farm.

farms.name: Super Smelter (furnace array)
farms.principle: Items and fuel are split across many furnaces by hoppers so smelting throughput scales with furnace count; outputs merge back into one chest.
caveats: Use blast furnaces for ores/metals (2x speed) and regular furnaces for food/logs; balance fuel distribution.

farms.name: Item Sorting System
farms.principle: Hopper lines with comparator-read filter hoppers (item + 4 stacked filler items) divert each item type into its own storage, auto-sorting a whole farm network.
farms.rate: throughput = hopper speed (2.5 items/s per lane)
caveats: Each filter needs the target item + 4 non-stackable/other items to bias the comparator; add overflow handling for full chests.

farms.name: Bulk Storage System (with sorter + overflow)
farms.principle: A wall of double chests/barrels fed by an item sorter, with an overflow loop back to the input and a signal-strength full indicator, forms a scalable warehouse.
caveats: Design overflow so a full category doesn't back up the whole hopper line; comparators can drive a 'full' lamp.

farms.name: Villager Trading Hall (mending librarians)
farms.principle: Isolated villagers are assigned lecterns and re-rolled until they offer wanted trades (Mending, Silk Touch, etc.); cheap emerald trades and enchanted books flow from a stall array.
caveats: Trade prices scale with demand and were rebalanced in the 1.21 line; re-roll unemployed librarians by breaking/replacing the lectern until the desired book appears.

farms.name: Auto-Crafter Array (1.21 Crafter)
farms.principle: The Crafter block, pulsed by redstone and fed by hoppers, auto-crafts recipes (rails, sticks, paper, dyes, food) turning raw farm output into finished items.
caveats: Crafter (added 1.21) enables fully-automatic crafting; use a comparator on the crafter to only fire when the grid is full.

farms.name: Block Compactor (ingots -> blocks)
farms.principle: A Crafter fed 9-at-a-time compresses ingots/nuggets/resources into blocks (iron/gold/copper/etc.) to save storage space and simplify transport.
caveats: Only fires when 9 items fill the grid (comparator on crafter); great tail-end for iron/gold farms.

farms.name: Automatic Brewing Station
farms.principle: Hoppers and droppers feed brewing stands in sequence (water bottles, nether wart, then the effect ingredient and gunpowder/redstone), auto-producing stacks of potions.
caveats: Sequence matters: nether wart first (awkward potion), then the effect ingredient, then modifiers (redstone/glowstone/gunpowder). Blaze powder fuels the stand.

farms.name: Wandering Trader Farm/Trap
farms.principle: Wandering traders that spawn near the player are trapped and killed for leads (and their llamas), a renewable source of leads and rare plants via trades.
caveats: Killing a leashed trader llama or trader drops leads; spawn rate is slow and tied to the wandering trader spawn cycle.

farms.name: Mob Switch (cap filler)
farms.principle: A large group of persistent mobs is kept loaded far away to fill a spawn category's mob cap, stopping natural spawns elsewhere so targeted farms (or perimeters) run at full rate.
farms.y_level: loaded but out of the way
caveats: Technical control device; only affects the chosen cap category. Some servers restrict chunk-loaders. Name-tag or otherwise persist the mobs.

farms.name: Nether Portal Item Transport
farms.principle: Items dropped through a linked nether portal traverse the 8:1 distance instantly in the other dimension; a hopper/dropper stream ships farm output across huge distances cheaply.
caveats: Portal linking must be precise so items arrive at the intended receiver; a collection water stream + hoppers catch items on the far side.

farms.name: TNT/Flying-Machine Tunnel Bore
farms.principle: A flying machine pushes TNT/instant-mine heads through stone, clearing large tunnels or perimeters; drops are swept up for bulk stone/ore and cleared spawn perimeters.
caveats: TNT-based bores rely on TNT duplication; disabled on many servers. Used to dig perimeters for high-rate mob/gold farms.

farms.name: Auto Shulker Box Loader/Unloader
farms.principle: Hoppers fill shulker boxes to a set count (comparator) then a piston/dispenser cycles a fresh box; a matching unloader empties boxes back into storage — bulk transport packaging.
caveats: Pairs with a shulker farm for endless boxes; comparator detects a full box before ejecting it.

farms.name: Auto Food Smoker (cooked food)
farms.principle: Smokers cook raw meat/food at double speed; hoppers feed raw food from animal farms and pull cooked food to storage, closing the food loop automatically.
caveats: Smokers only cook food items (2x speed); use dried kelp blocks or charcoal as renewable fuel.

farms.name: Zombie Villager Curing Station (cheap trades)
farms.principle: Zombie villagers are cured with a splash Potion of Weakness + golden apple; a cured villager gives massive permanent trade discounts, making enchanted books/gear cheap.
caveats: Discount from repeated curing was capped/rebalanced in recent versions, but a single cure still gives strong permanent discounts. Keep the villager near the cure spot (gossip range).

farms.name: Magma Cube Farm
farms.principle: Magma cubes spawn on large flat nether platforms (best in basalt deltas / nether wastes); big cubes split into small ones which are pushed to a kill for magma cream.
farms.y_level: on a flat nether plane / roof
caveats: Magma cubes ignore light; big cubes must be allowed room to split into small cubes (which drop the cream). Basalt deltas has the highest magma-cube spawn weight.

farms.name: Ghast Farm
farms.principle: Ghasts need a large open air volume to spawn; a big spawn-proofed platform in soul sand valley / nether wastes lets ghasts spawn and be funneled to a kill for ghast tears and gunpowder.
caveats: Ghasts require a 5x5x5 empty space to spawn, so rates are low; soul sand valley has the best ghast spawn weight.

farms.name: Husk Farm (desert)
farms.principle: Husks spawn in place of zombies on desert surfaces at night; a dark desert-biome platform funnels them to a dry kill (no water, or they convert to drowned) for rotten flesh and gear.
caveats: Husks only spawn in desert biomes; keep the kill dry so they don't convert into drowned. Great emerald source via rotten-flesh cleric trades.

farms.name: Perimeter Spawn-Proofing Setup
farms.principle: Every cave/surface within 128 blocks of a sky mob/gold farm is lit or slabbed so the mob cap isn't wasted on random spawns — the single biggest rate multiplier for any spawn-based farm.
caveats: Digging/lighting a full perimeter is a big project but can multiply a mob/gold farm's rate several times over.
